title: Nilpotent fibre criterion for flat modules
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$. Let $M$ be an $A$-module, regarded as an $R$-module by restriction of scalars. Write $IA$ for the ideal generated by the image of $I$ and $IM$ for the submodule generated by the products $im$, so $M/IM$ is an $A/IA$-module. If $M$ is flat over $R$ and $M/IM$ is flat over $A/IA$, then $M$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No finite-generation, finite-presentation, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06A5 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-nilpotent), first conclusion, with S=A and S prime=A.

proof.text: Write $f:R\to A$ for the given map and $J=IA$. Since $I\hookrightarrow R$ is injective and $M$ is $R$-flat, the map $I\otimes_R M\to R\otimes_R M$ is injective by the definition of flatness. The mutually inverse maps $R\otimes_R M\to M$, $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, and $M\to R\otimes_R M$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, identify its composite with $\mu_R:I\otimes_R M\to M$, $i\otimes m\mapsto f(i)m$. Thus $\mu_R$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 06A5, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-nilpotent, proof of the first conclusion (S=A and S prime=A).

proof.text: The tensor universal property defines an $R$-linear map $\theta:I\otimes_R M\to J\otimes_A M$, $i\otimes m\mapsto f(i)\otimes m$. It is surjective: every element of the target is a finite sum of pure tensors, and every $j\in J$ is a finite sum $j=\sum_t a_t f(i_t)$ with $a_t\in A$, $i_t\in I$. The balancing relation gives $j\otimes m=\sum_t f(i_t)\otimes a_tm=\theta(\sum_t i_t\otimes a_tm)$.

source.place: Tag 06A5, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-nilpotent, proof of the first conclusion (S=A and S prime=A).

proof.text: The multiplication map $\mu_A:J\otimes_A M\to M$, $j\otimes m\mapsto jm$, is defined by the tensor universal property, and $\mu_A\theta=\mu_R$ on pure tensors, hence everywhere. If $\mu_A(z)=0$, lift $z=\theta(y)$ by step 2. Then $\mu_R(y)=0$, so $y=0$ by step 1 and $z=0$. Thus $\mu_A$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 06A5, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-nilpotent, proof of the first conclusion (S=A and S prime=A).

proof.text: The ideal $J$ is nilpotent: expand a product of $N$ sums of generators $a f(i)$ of $J$; every term is an $A$-multiple of $f(i_1\cdots i_N)=0$ since $I^N=0$. Thus $J^N=0$. Moreover $JM=IM$: each generator $f(i)m$ of $IM$ lies in $JM$, while $a f(i)m=f(i)(am)$ shows that every generator of $JM$ lies in $IM$. Hence the given flat $A/IA$-module $M/IM$ is exactly $M/JM$.

source.place: Tag 06A5, lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-nilpotent, proof of the first conclusion (S=A and S prime=A).

proof.text: Apply the cited nilpotent-ideal flatness criterion to the ring $A$, ideal $J$ and module $M$. Step 4 gives $J^N=0$ and flatness of $M/JM$ over $A/J$; step 3 gives injectivity of $J\otimes_A M\to M$. Its conclusion is that $M$ is flat over $A$, with none of the finiteness hypotheses excluded by the item.
